sample_frame: vendor-selected active channels indexed via YouTube Data API, not probability-sampled global channel population

independent_channel_age_results.faceless_classification: vendor inferred from titles descriptions and presentation; not authoritative YouTube category

valid_comparisons: Long-form and Shorts 5x percentages use same provider-relative channel-and-format definition, but cannot be treated as causal format effects or universal YouTube video probabilities.
The 555,158 scored-videos denominator is distinct from 558,739 indexed video objects; 3,581 missing comparison values must not be silently treated as failed breakouts.
A 5x breakout is views relative to the same channel's historical same-format median, not 5x other channels or high absolute audience and not 5x monetary income.
A channel below 10,000 subscribers is not necessarily a recently created channel; newness by age and size must not be conflated.
Niche-specific numerators of small channels with any 5x video lack total sampled small-channel niche denominators, so success percentages by niche cannot be derived.
Vendor-enter-now labels, ranks, and score values are commercial proprietary selections, not validated opportunity probabilities.
Monetization signals or estimated faceless identity do not prove accepted YPP applications, net profit or available creator payroll.
Current public view counts and long-lived video histories need temporal metric-definition harmonization before longitudinal causal analysis.

length_bins.publisher_section: Longer videos break out more often
length_bins.binning_note: Publisher labels the discussion 'long-form', but includes videos under one minute; classification of under-one-minute objects as Shorts or ordinary uploads is not published.
notes: Proportions are vendor-indexed video events above own channel's same-format median, not a population probability and not sustained creator revenue.
The 40-minute bin may mix channel maturity, topic, languages, retention and production costs; no controlled comparison.
No published n per bin, uncertainty intervals, same-video-age adjustment, per-bin monetization, labor or ad inventory.
The independently official eight-minute mid-roll slot *eligibility* gate falls inside the vendor's 4-to-10-minute bucket, whose 9.3% breakout proportion says nothing about mid-roll ad serving.
The vendor's under-one-minute bin is not automatically comparable to a long-form-only analysis because the report does not document its Shorts cutoff or per-bin video classification.
